Subject: Management Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2016 (Audited)  
 
To:  The President  
  The Stock Exchange of Thailand 
 
 Kiatnakin Bank Public Company Limited (“the Bank” or “KK”) submits the Management 
Discussion and Analysis (MD&A) report for the year ended December 31, 2016 , comparing operating 
performance and financial position for the y ear 2016 with those of  2015. This report discusses principal 
changes in the audited consolidated financial statements. 
 
Overall market environment 
 The Thai economy for the year 2016 is expected to grow at 3.2%, increased from growth of 2.8% 
during the year 2015 with contributions from the following key factors  1) Continuous growth in tourism 
sector with the number of tourists arrivals continuing to expand at 8.9% together with various year -end 
stimulus measures such as exemption of visa fees, tax privil ege for domestic travels etc. aimed at 
lessening the impact from  the recent measures to curb illegitimate tour operators 2) Increased in public 
spending together with various economic stimulus initiatives; year -end tax privilege for Baht 15,000 
domestic consumption, payment to low -income non-agricultural related individuals 3) Gra dual recovery 
in the agricultural sector especially during the second half of 2016 after the impact from the drought has 
tapered off and the continued increase in agricultural pr ices for petroleum -related products 4)  Signs of 
recovery in the export sector partly from the increased in oil prices and the brightening prospect for the 
electronics market segment. Nevertheless, the structural problems of the Thai economy still limit the  
economic growth as can be seen from the following factors: Capacity utilization still remains at a low 
level limiting investment growth in the private sector. The continuous decline in employment rate 
together with the current high level of household debt  both of which impede the recovery of private 
consumption. For the year 2017, t he Bank in-house research projected the domestic economic growth to 
be at 3.2% the same level as that of the previous year. 
 For financial market, The Bank of Thailand maintaine d the policy rate at 1.5%, the same level 
since April 2015. Inflation currently below the target level is projected to return to be within the target 
band of 1.00% - 4.00% within 1Q17.

2 
 
The auto industry for the year 2016 still exhibited a continual contraction for 4 consecutive years, 
with the number of new car sales for the year 2016 totaling 768,788 units, a contraction of 3.9% yoy. 
Sales for passenger car segment declined 6.5% yoy while the commercial vehicle segment registered a 
smaller contraction of 2.3%. This is partly due to the increased in demand for pick -up trucks and pick-up 
passenger vehicles (PPV) contributed by the improvement in the agricultural sector in the second half of 
2016. Based  on the Bank in -house research, new car sales for the yea r 2017 is projected to slightly 
increase with total sales of around 790,000 units. 
In the equity market, the average daily turnover (SET and mai) for the year 2016 increased from 
Baht 44,302 million in 2015 to Baht 52,526 million , an increase of 18.6%.  The SET index at the end of 
2016, closed at 1,542.94 points, improving by 19.8% from 1,288.02 points at the end of 2015. 
 
Overall Business Operations for the year 2016 
 
The Bank’s loan portfolio for the year 2016 contracted slightly  by 0.8 % from the end of 2015 
comparing to contractions of 3.6% in 2015 and contractions of 3.1% in 2014.  Key contributions to the 
year 2016  loan growth are from the  following: Lombard loan s increased by 208.2%, personnel loans 
increased by 105.0%, Micro SMEs including SME Car3x loans expanded at 90.7% while housing loans 
expanded at 289.5%. Meanwhile, hire purchase loans and commercial loans contracted by 2.7% and 
10.6% respectively for the year. Corporate banking loans also declined by 21.6% for the year 2016. 
For asset quality, t he Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) to total loans ratio at the end of 2016 
decreased to 5.6% from 5.8% at the end of 2015 . The NPLs from l oans to real estate developments 
segment improved slightly during the year while NPLs for hire purchase loans continued to show 
continuous improvement with the NPLs ratio for hire purchase loans still in a decline from 2.4% at the 
end of 2015 to 1.9% at the end of 2016.  During 2016, t he Bank issued total debentures amounting to 
Baht 91,173 million, of which Baht 3,000 million are subordinated debentures classified as Tier 2 capital. 
On Special Asset Management business, the Bank sold non-performing assets (NPAs) totaling Baht 2,633 
million and had gain of Baht 1,189 million.  
For the year 2016, the Bank has outlined the following 3 key business areas of focus 1) Credit 
House – building efficiencies and creating standards, loan expansions and effective credit monitoring and 
control 2) Private Banking – business expansions, capitalizing on th e Kiatnakin Phatra Financial Group  
(“the Group”) expertise in the business to expand and increase fee income and assets under advise and 3) 
Investment Banking – maintaining the status as the leader in Investment Banking . In addition to the three 
business areas of focus, the Bank plan s to capitalize on collaborations within the G roup to expand the 
products and services offerings while enhancing business processes with an aim to offer seamless services 
between Banking and Capital market business. The Bank wil l continue to focus on developing new 
products and services while expanding to new customer base through new alternative channels for 
example, through direct sale agents, to extend the Bank reach to retail customers.

3 
 
Key developments during 2016 are as following: s ubsequent to Phatra Capital Public Company 
Limited (“Phatra”), a subsidiary in which the Bank holds 99.98% of the shares, has executed a sale and 
purchase agreement for the sale of all shares in KKTRADE Securities Company Limited (“kktrade”) with 
Yuanta Securities Asia Financial Services Limited  (“Yuanta”) (the “Share Sale and Purchase 
Agreement”). The material detail  of the Share Sale and Purchase Agreement are as stated in the Bank ’s 
letter to The Stock Exchange of Thailand dated April 27, 2016. Subsequently, on July 8, 2016, the parties 
have fulfilled all conditions precedent under the Share Sale and Purchase Agreement and Phatra has 
completed the sale of shares in kktrade to Yuanta under the terms and conditions of the Share Sale and 
Purchase Agreement. 
Additionally, in order to expand the Group financial and investment services and products in 
relation to the Group’s wealth management service, the Bank has established Phatra  Asset Management 
(Cayman) Limited to support the Group operation of securities investment business overseas.  
On products and services, the Bank introduced “KK SME Car 3x” loan, aimed at small and 
medium-sized enterprises, using cars as collateral with ma ximum credit line of three times the collateral 
value. For  deposit and investment products, the Bank launched “Phatra Edge”, an investment and 
financial planning service to clients with deposits and investments accounts between Baht 2 -30 million. 
The Bank also launched “KK e -Banking” to provide the Bank’s customers with added convenience 
through the use of secured on -line financial management and services. KK e -Banking services are 
available through both website and mobile application format.  
In terms of distribution channels, the Bank direct sales team which was recently set up in order to 
expand the Bank’s customer base to new customer groups for personal loans, housing loans and SME Car 
3x products, has been in full operations during 2016 and has been e xpanding the Bank’s reach into the 
new customer groups as planned. Additionally, during 4Q16, the Bank has opened 1 new branch at 
CentralPlaza Ladprao in addition to the Bank’s financial hubs at Central World shopping complex and at 
Thonglor road which were opened earlier during 2016. The financial hub exhibits the Bank’s new branch 
model concept with a focus on providing comprehensive financial and investment services to the Bank’s 
customers. As of the end of December 2016, the Bank has a total of 66 branches. 
For Capital market business, t he market shares (SET and mai excluding proprietary trading) of 
Phatra Securities Plc. (PSEC) was 4.81%, increased from 4.69 % in 2015, ranking 4th from total 36 
brokers.

Operating results of the Bank and subsidiaries for the year 2016 comparing with the year 2015 
 The consolidated net profit for year 2016 totaled Baht 5,547 million, an increase of 67.2% yoy, 
of which Baht 1,086 million was the net profit from Capital Market Business operated by Phatra Capital 
Plc. (Phatra), and subsidiaries i.e. PSEC  and PASSET. Meanwhile, the consolidated comprehensive 
income for 2016 totaled Baht 5,756 million, increased by 84.6% yoy. T he Capital Market b usiness 
comprehensive income was Baht 1,075 million. The comprehensive income included revaluation of 
available-for-sale securities as a result of the capital market volatility. 
Interest income  was Baht 14,869 million, increased by 0.6% yoy mainly from the increase in 
interest income on investment in loans by 84.3% yoy from loan restructuring progress. Meanwhile, 
interest income on loans declined by 4.3% mainly as a result of the contraction in commercial loans 
portfolio for the real estate development segment during the year . Interest income from securities also 
declined by 30.3%.

 Net fee s and service s income totaled Baht 3,707 million, in creasing by 6.8% from 2015. For

and underwriting fees totaled Baht 171 million, declining by 28.3% yoy. Bancassurance fee amounted to

Total operating income amounted to Baht 16,156 million, increased by 7.3% yoy mainly from the 
increase in net interest income  of 10.4% together with the increase in net fee s and services income by 
6.8% as stated  above. Meanwhile, the Bank recorded  gain on trading and foreign exchange transactions 
mainly contributed from the Capital Market business in the amount of Baht 577 million, decreasing 
34.2% yoy. The Bank also re corded gain on investments totaled Baht 203 million, a decrease of 39.4% 
yoy. 
Other operating expenses  were Baht 7,352 million, decreased by 6.0% yoy. Other operating 
expenses also included loss  from sale of foreclosed assets , which in 2016 had a gain totaled Baht 545 
million, comparing to loss of Baht 381 million during 2015.   The gain on sale of foreclosed assets of 
Baht 545 million comprised of loss from sale of repossessed cars totaled Baht 644 million, declining 
47.4% yoy or reducing from loss of Baht 1,225 million in 2015 mainly from lower loss per asset cost with 
gain on sale of foreclosed properties totaled Baht 1,189 million, an increase of 40.9% comparing to gain 
of Baht 844 million in 2015. 
When excluding loss from sale of foreclosed assets and loss from revaluation of foreclosed assets, 
operating expenses for the year 2016 totaled Baht 7, 872 million increasing 12.2% yoy comparing to 
expenses of Baht 7,017 million for 201 5 with increases mainly from personnel expenses  and marketing 
expenses. Cost-to-income ratio excluding loss from sale of foreclosed assets and loss from r evaluations 
stood at 45.4% for 2016, comparing with 44.1% in 2015.

7 
 
Bad debts and doubtful accounts and loss on debt restructuring  totaled Baht 2,313 million, 
declining from Baht 3,208 million in 2015. During the year 2016, the Bank set up general reserve totaled 
Baht 1,650 million to provide buffer against economic uncertainties. 
Allowance for doubtful accounts  and allowance for troubled debt restructuring  amounted to Baht 
10,966 million with outstanding Baht 4,500 million in general reserve. The total loan loss reserve to total 
mandatory reserve ratio increased to 187.8% comparing to 160.1% at the end of 2015. Meanwhile, total 
loan loss reserve  to total NPLs ratio (coverage ratio) is at 110.1%, increasing from 91.9% at the end of 
2015. 
  Corporate Income Tax totaled Baht 879 million or 13.5% tax rate. Basic earnings per share and

Operating results of the Bank and subsidiaries for 4Q16 comparing with 4Q15 
The consolidated net profit for 4Q16 totaled Baht 1,452 million, increased by 48.1% comparing 
to the same period last year , of which Baht 216 million was the net profit from Capital Market b usiness 
operated by Phatra Capital Plc. (Phat ra) and subsidiaries i.e.  PSEC and PASSET. Meanwhile, the 
consolidated comprehensive income totaled Baht 1,255 million, increased by 22.5% with Capital Market 
business comprehensive income at Baht 295 million. The comprehensive income included revaluation of 
available-for-sale securities as a result of the capital market volatility. 
Net interest income amounted to Baht 2,602 million, up 1.3% following improving loan spread 
from 5.1% in 4Q15 to 5.5% in 4Q16. Yield on loan improved slightly to 7.9% from 7.8% yoy while cost 
of fund declined from 2.7% in 4Q15 to 2.4% in 4Q16.  
Net fee and service income  totaled Baht 1,014 million, increasing 6.1% yoy mainly from the 
increase in financial advisory and underwriting fee which for 4Q16 totaled Baht 133 million or an 
increase of 26.7% from  4Q15 and also from the increase in bancassurance fee  which totaled Baht 244 
million, increased by 9.3% yoy. Meanwhile, fee from Asset M anagement business fee totaled B aht 88 
million, a decline of 15.5% with brokerage fee also declining slightly by 1.8% yoy.

8 
 
Total operating income  amounted to Baht 4,161 million, a slight decrease of 1.0% from the 
same period last year . During 4Q16, net interest income and net fees and services income increased as 
outlined above, however, gain on trading and foreign exchange  transactions amounted to Baht 160 
million, decreasing 59.2% yoy. Gain on investments also declined by Baht 44 million from 4Q15. 
Other operating expenses were Baht 2,430 million, increased by 5.6% yoy. Loss from sale of 
foreclosed assets during 4Q16 totaled Baht 173 million, comparing to gain of Baht 20 million during the 
same period last year with loss from sale of repossessed cars totaled Baht 208 million and gain on sale of 
foreclosed properties totaled Baht 35 million for 4Q16. 
When excluding loss from sale of foreclosed assets and loss from revaluation of foreclosed assets, 
operating expenses for 4Q16 totaled Baht 2,214 million increasing 6.7% yoy comparing to expenses of 
Baht 2,074 million for 4Q15. Cost-to-income ratio excluding loss from sale of for eclosed assets and loss 
from revaluations stood at 52.8% for 4Q16, comparing with 46.4% in 4Q15. 
Bad debts and doubtful accounts and loss on debt restructuring  totaled Baht 100 million, 
decreasing from Baht 824 million yoy. For the year 2016, the Bank set up additional general reserve of 
Baht 350 million in 1Q16, Baht 300 million in 2Q16 , Baht 750 million in 3Q16  and Baht 250 million in 
4Q16, totaling Baht 1,650 million.

The Dividend payment

business, by Direct Investment Department (“DI”), with medium to long -term investment horizon, while 
PSEC manages short -term investment, by Investment and Trading Gr oup, comprising of Equity and

structured products. HF focuses on equity and derivatives trading with less than 1 year investment 
horizon, applying Market Neutral strategy and advanced statistical modeling.
